captions.instagram:
How do screenplays and storyboards work?

Before a camera rolls, a film already exists twice: as a script where one page is about one minute, and as a comic strip of every shot. Write a scene, board it from a 3D camera, cross the 180-degree line and play your own animatic.

→ Every film starts as a screenplay, typed in the same strict layout.
→ The layout makes a handy rule: one page is about one minute on screen.
→ Most films follow three acts, with the tension climbing to a climax.
→ Indian films add an interval, with a huge twist right before it.
→ A storyboard turns each line of script into a drawing of one shot.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/storyboardclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do screenplays and storyboards work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Before a camera rolls, a film already exists twice: as a script where one page is about one minute, and as a comic strip of every shot. Write a scene, board it from a 3D camera, cross the 180-degree line and play your own animatic.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/storyboardclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/storyboardclear

In this video:
• A script is a timed blueprint. Screenplays use 12-point Courier and fixed margins for headings, action, names and dialogue, so one page runs about one minute.
• Stories have a shape. Most films follow three acts: set-up, confrontation, resolution, with turning points that push the tension up to a climax.
• Words become pictures. A storyboard draws every shot.
• Coverage and the line. A scene is filmed from several set-ups: a master, over-the-shoulders and close-ups.
• Timing before shooting. An animatic plays the panels in time with temp sound.
• You direct. Board a six-shot scene yourself.
